items.passage: Why does a man wear a hat indoors? My daughter, Priya, asked this of Mayor Marlon one wet afternoon in the drying shed of the tea estate above Surabaya, where I had come, as the town's only doctor, to discuss the fever in the pickers' quarters. Marlon laughed and tipped the wide straw brim lower. He told me the clinic would get its new beds after the harvest, the same promise he had made after the last harvest. Each time I pressed him on the numbers, he adjusted the hat, and its shadow slid across his eyes like a shutter. Later, walking down between the rows, Priya said she thought he must have been cold. I told her yes, perhaps. But I had noticed that when the estate owner arrived in his car, Marlon took the hat off at once and held it against his chest, his face suddenly bare and eager.
items.question: Based on the text, the mayor's hat most likely represents which of the following?
options: The authority Marlon holds over the pickers and the clinic
Marlon's habit of concealing himself from people he owes
The damp, chilly weather that fills the drying shed
Marlon's embarrassment at being questioned by a child
items.explanation: Marlon은 의사가 숫자를 따질 때마다 모자를 고쳐 써 그림자로 눈을 가리고, 약속은 매번 미뤄진다. 반면 농장주가 오자 즉시 모자를 벗고 맨얼굴을 드러낸다. 두 장면을 연결하면 모자는 자신에게 책임을 묻는 사람들 앞에서 자신을 숨기는 태도를 나타내므로 B가 정답이다. A는 권위를, C는 Priya의 순진한 해석을, D는 아이의 질문만을 근거로 한 오답이다.

items.passage: “He would have come, Yuying, if the river had let him,” Camryn says, and you do not believe him. The wedding hall is so crowded that the fiddlers must lean back against the wall, yet beside you one chair stands empty, a white card propped upon it bearing your father's name. You remember the letter from the conservatory in Memphis, the one that arrived the spring your father took the family savings downriver and did not return. Camryn had travelled with him that spring; you have always held him half to blame. Now he rests his hand upon the empty chair as he speaks, the way a man steadies himself against a rail. When the dancing begins and a cousin tries to borrow the chair, Camryn stops her gently. Leave it, he tells her. You notice that his own glass has stood untouched all evening, and that he will not look at the card.
items.question: Based on the text, the empty chair most likely symbolizes which of the following?
options: The narrator's lost chance to study at the conservatory
The crowding of the hall and the family's lack of money
An unresolved loss that weighs on Camryn as well as Yuying
Camryn's wish to take the father's place in the family
items.explanation: 빈 의자에는 떠나 돌아오지 않은 아버지의 이름표가 놓여 있고, Yuying은 그 일로 Camryn을 탓해 왔다. 그런데 Camryn은 의자에 기대듯 손을 얹고, 사촌이 의자를 가져가려 하자 막으며, 술잔도 건드리지 않은 채 이름표를 보지 못한다. 이 단서들을 이으면 의자는 두 사람 모두가 떨치지 못한 상실을 상징하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 아버지의 부재가 낳은 결과 하나만 본 것이고, B와 D는 지문의 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Three rules governed the old weaving house in Lisbon, and you learned them on your first day: no lamp after midnight, no cloth cut before it is finished, and no news spoken until it is certain. Rafaela, who had bought the house that winter, kept all three. Each morning she climbed to the loom room while Mateo, the gardener, pruned the lemon trees below, and each morning she wove one more row of a blue cloth with no pattern anyone could name. The ship carrying her brother was weeks overdue. When Mateo asked why she did not weave something useful, a shawl or a blanket, she only said that the cloth was not finished. Rows gathered like days. Once, when a rumor of a wreck came up the hill, her hands stopped above the threads for a full hour; then she tied the next knot and went on. By midsummer, Mateo had begun bringing her a sprig of lemon blossom each dawn and laying it, without a word, beside the growing blue.
items.question: Based on the text, the blue cloth most likely represents which of the following?
options: Rafaela's wish to make the old house useful again
The strict household rules that came with the house
The friendship slowly forming between Rafaela and Mateo
Rafaela's refusal to stop expecting her brother's return
items.explanation: Rafaela는 오빠의 배가 늦어지는 동안 매일 한 줄씩 천을 짜고, 끝나기 전에는 자르지 않는다는 규칙을 지킨다. 난파 소문에 한 시간 멈췄다가도 다시 매듭을 묶는 장면은 희망을 놓지 않는 태도를 보여 준다. 따라서 천은 오빠의 귀환을 계속 기다리는 마음을 상징하며 D가 정답이다. A는 Mateo의 제안을, B는 규칙 자체를, C는 마지막 장면의 꽃만을 근거로 한 그럴듯한 오답이다.

items.passage: Years later, Rangi would still remember the evening his son refused to leave the gymnasium in Lyon. It was the anniversary of Elodie's death, and Rangi had planned a quiet dinner at the restaurant she had loved. The boy, fourteen and immovable, had other ideas: he wanted to shoot free throws in the empty gym where his mother had once coached, one for every year since she had been gone. Rangi argued, then pleaded, then sat on the bottom bleacher with his coat still buttoned. His son did not answer. He simply kept shooting, building a wall of silence brick by brick with every bounce of the ball. Only on the fifth shot, when the ball rolled away toward the bleachers, did Rangi stand, pick it up, and pass it back.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “building a wall of silence brick by brick” most nearly suggests that the son
options: was damaging the gymnasium in his anger at his father
was growing too tired to keep arguing with his father
was shutting out his father's objections through steady repetition
was quietly showing off his skill to win his father's praise
items.explanation: 아들은 아버지의 설득과 애원에 대답하지 않고, 공을 튀길 때마다 침묵을 한 겹씩 더한다. '벽돌을 한 장씩 쌓는다'는 비유는 같은 동작의 반복으로 아버지의 반대를 차단하는 모습을 나타내므로 C가 정답이다. A는 벽을 문자 그대로 받아들인 해석이고, B와 D는 지문에 피로나 과시의 단서가 없다. 아버지가 결국 공을 건네주는 결말도 아들이 쌓은 벽을 아버지가 받아들였음을 보여 준다.

items.passage: Night is honest. In the sanatorium above the lake outside Bergen, I learned that patients say at two in the morning what they hide by daylight. Thorvald, my night patient, could not sleep unless I wheeled him to the end of the dock, where the water lay black and still. On the fourth night he showed me an envelope addressed to his brother, sealed and stamped and eleven years old. He had written it the week after their quarrel. He never mailed it, he said, and his brother had died the following spring. He held it on his blanket while he talked, and I understood that the apology had become an anchor he dragged behind him, slowing every hour he had left. Before dawn he asked me, Sigrid, to keep it for him. I put it in my apron pocket, where it weighed almost nothing.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “an anchor he dragged behind him” most nearly suggests that the unsent apology was
options: a source of steadiness that kept Thorvald calm at night
a memory Thorvald was ready to throw into the lake
a hope of reconciliation that still guided his choices
a weight of regret that kept holding Thorvald back
items.explanation: Thorvald는 형과 다툰 뒤 쓴 사과 편지를 11년 동안 부치지 못했고, 형은 이미 세상을 떠났다. 화자는 그 사과가 남은 시간을 늦추며 끌고 다니는 닻이 되었다고 말하는데, 이는 그를 붙잡는 후회의 무게를 뜻하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 닻의 '안정' 의미에 끌린 오답이고, B와 C는 형의 죽음으로 화해의 가능성이 사라졌다는 점과 맞지 않는다. 편지를 Sigrid에게 맡기자 거의 무게가 없었다는 대비도 이 해석을 뒷받침한다.

items.passage:
Who pays a clockmaker for the hours he gives away?
My father, Santiago, bent above his bench
on Forty-Third Street, where the trains shook dust
from the rafters into every open case.
Ottavio came in winter with a watch
his wife had worn, its mainspring broken, its glass
clouded like a frozen pond.
He counted out his nickels on the counter.
My father pushed them back without a word
and worked past closing, past supper, past the lamps,
spending his minutes like coins on a stranger
while I translated nothing, for nothing needed saying.
When the watch ticked, Ottavio wept in Italian.
My father answered him in Spanish.
I stood between them with my English,
the only one who thought words were required.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “spending his minutes like coins on a stranger” most nearly suggests that Santiago was
options: giving his own time freely in place of taking payment
wasting time carelessly on a repair he did not value
charging Ottavio for every minute of his labor
hurrying to finish the repair so he could close
items.explanation: Santiago는 Ottavio가 내민 동전을 말없이 돌려주고, 가게 문을 닫은 뒤에도 늦게까지 시계를 고친다. 그러므로 '분을 동전처럼 쓴다'는 비유는 돈 대신 자기 시간을 선물처럼 내어 주었다는 뜻이며 A가 정답이다. C는 동전이라는 단어에 끌린 오답이고, B와 D는 정성껏 오래 일한 장면과 어긋난다. 첫 행의 질문도 대가 없이 내어 준 시간이라는 주제를 미리 보여 준다.

items.passage: Are you the ranger, or are you lost too? That was the first thing Shanice asked me, and I have never answered it honestly. I had found her at dusk on the trail above Port of Spain, ankle twisted, map soaked, and I walked her down to the only shelter I knew: the courtyard of my grandmother's house, where a stone fountain stood in the middle like a guest who had stopped talking. My grandmother had begun restoring it the year before she died. The pipes were half laid; a bag of mortar had hardened into a boulder beside the basin. Shanice sat on its rim and asked why it was dry. I told her about the parts I could not find and the plumber who never called back. She listened, then said, Roshane, it looks like a throat that has forgotten how to sing. I laughed, but that night I went out with a flashlight and counted the missing fittings.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a throat that has forgotten how to sing” most nearly suggests that the fountain is
options: an object too badly damaged ever to be repaired
a structure that has lost the function that gave it life
a reminder of the grandmother's beautiful voice
a place where neighbors once gathered to talk
items.explanation: 분수는 할머니가 복원하다 멈춘 채 말라 있고, 부품이 빠진 탓에 물이 흐르지 않는다. 노래를 잊은 목이라는 비유는 본래 물을 뿜던 기능을 잃어 생기를 잃은 상태를 가리키므로 B가 정답이다. A는 화자가 그날 밤 빠진 부품을 세며 복원 가능성을 확인하는 장면과 맞지 않는다. C와 D는 목소리와 말이라는 연상에 기댄 오답으로 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Four hours a day, six days a week, no recordings: those were Ananya's conditions when she agreed to teach me. We met in the guesthouse of a small monastery on the edge of Mumbai, where the monks let her use a whitewashed room in exchange for playing at their evening prayers. She taught a way of tuning and bowing that her own teacher had learned in a village whose name I could not find on any map. Nobody else I knew played like that anymore. When I asked why she would not let me record her, she said a tape would teach my ears but not my hands. Vikram, she would say, again, and correct my wrist with a pencil tap until I hated the sound of it. Only much later did I see that the old style lived in her fingers like a language with one speaker left.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a language with one speaker left” most nearly suggests that the old style was
options: a technique so complex that it needed translation
a kind of music Ananya refused to share with others
a rare practice kept alive almost entirely by one person
a habit Ananya found difficult to explain in words
items.explanation: 지문은 그 연주법이 지도에도 없는 마을에서 전해졌고 이제 그렇게 연주하는 사람이 거의 없다고 말한다. 따라서 화자 한 명만 남은 언어라는 비유는 거의 한 사람에 의해서만 이어지는 사라져 가는 기술을 뜻하며 C가 정답이다. A는 '언어'를 번역과 연결한 오답이고, B는 녹음을 거부한 점만 보고 Ananya가 직접 가르친다는 사실을 놓친 것이다. D는 그녀가 말 대신 손으로 가르친 장면을 지나치게 해석한 것이다.

items.passage: So you let me win, Edith said, the moment Faisal stepped onto the old stone bridge. They had not spoken in nine years, not since the summer their grandmother set them to race across the Cornish headland for her silver whistle. Faisal had been faster; everyone knew it. Yet a stride from the bridge he had stumbled, and Edith had touched the parapet first. Now the grandmother lay in the churchyard behind them, and the whistle hung at Edith's neck. All these years, she said, the prize had felt like borrowed bread, filling her mouth but never her stomach. Faisal looked down at the river. He told her he had seen how badly she needed something of her own that year. Edith unhooked the whistle and pressed it into his palm, and for once he did not give it back.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “borrowed bread” most nearly suggests that Edith's victory was
options: a gift she had been eager to return to her grandmother long ago
a reward she had always been required to share with Faisal
a prize whose value faded slowly as she grew older
a win she could not fully enjoy because it was not earned
items.explanation: Edith는 더 빠른 Faisal이 결승 직전에 일부러 넘어져 이겼다는 사실을 알고 있었다. 빌린 빵이 입은 채워도 배는 채우지 못했다는 표현은 스스로 얻지 않은 승리라 진정한 만족을 주지 못했다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 할머니에게 돌려주려 했다는 근거가 없고, B는 '빌렸다'를 공유로 오해한 것이다. C는 시간이 흐르며 가치가 줄었다는 해석으로, 처음부터 공허했다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Two jars of dye, one bolt of linen, and no papers: that was everything Stavros carried to the customs checkpoint outside Thessaloniki, and the officer wanted to know why. The dye was the problem. Emre, the old tailor who had trained him for six years, mixed its deep pomegranate red by smell and by the color of the steam, and he had refused every request to set the recipe on paper. When the officer demanded a list of ingredients, Stavros could offer only what he had watched over Emre's shoulder: a handful of something, a pinch of something else, a boil until it looked right. His account was so ______ that the officer finally waved him through, convinced that no smuggler would invent anything so vague and so sincere.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: fragmentary
elaborate
rehearsed
technical
items.explanation: 조리법은 한 번도 글로 적힌 적이 없고, Stavros는 어깨 너머로 본 '한 줌, 한 꼬집' 같은 조각만 말할 수 있었다. 관리가 그 설명을 '모호하다'고 여겼다는 점까지 연결하면 빈칸에는 단편적이라는 뜻의 A가 가장 알맞다. B와 D는 모호함과 정반대이고, C는 '진심 어린' 설명이라는 단서와 충돌한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다.

items.passage: Once, in the summer of my nineteenth year, I spent a whole night in the dining hall of a children's camp outside Hamburg, waiting with a stranger for a storm to clear the road. Her name was Liesel, and she was travelling, she told me, to a position as governess that she dreaded. Toward midnight the camp director came in with a lantern and announced that a carriage bound back to the city had room for one passenger. Liesel looked at the door a long while. Here was her chance to turn back with no excuse required and no one to blame but the weather. Yet when the director turned to her, she ______ the offer, folding her hands as if to hold herself in place, and said that she had given her word. I, Friedrich, who had made no such promise, took the seat myself.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: welcomed
declined
weighed
seized
items.explanation: Liesel은 두려운 일자리로 가는 중이었지만, 손을 모아 자신을 붙잡듯 하며 약속을 했다고 말한다. 게다가 결국 그 자리에 Friedrich가 탔으므로 그녀는 제안을 거절한 것이고 B가 정답이다. C는 문을 오래 바라본 장면 때문에 그럴듯하지만, 감독이 돌아본 순간의 최종 행동으로는 부족하다. A와 D는 제안을 받아들였다는 뜻이라 결말과 모순된다.

items.passage:
Rivers do not wait.
Daphne knew it, the ferryman's daughter,
who counted every passenger twice
as the barge slid past the bridges of Lima.
Haruo, who crossed each dusk with his tools,
watched her lips move, one, two, three,
then start again, as if the water
might steal a soul between the counts.
One evening he said nothing, only held
his palm out flat above the rail
and let the current lift a leaf from it.
She stopped at seven. Began again. Stopped.
By winter her counting had grown ______,
a murmur she forgot halfway through,
until one night the far shore arrived
and she had only watched the light.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: frantic
precise
faint
louder
items.explanation: Daphne는 승객을 두 번씩 세는 습관이 있었지만, Haruo가 잎을 물살에 놓아주는 모습을 본 뒤 세다가 멈추기 시작한다. 빈칸 뒤의 '중간에 잊어버리는 중얼거림'과 마지막에 빛만 바라보았다는 장면을 연결하면 습관이 희미해졌다는 C가 알맞다. A와 D는 습관이 더 강해졌다는 뜻이라 흐름과 반대이다. B는 원래의 꼼꼼한 세기를 떠올리게 하는 오답이다.

items.passage: Who opens a bakery in a cinema? That was the question half of Havana asked in the slow months of that year, when the picture house on the corner sat dark between seasons and its owner let Rosalinda sell bread from the lobby. Rosalinda had lost her shop to a fire; Eulalio, her rival of twenty years, had lost his to debt. Both had talked of leaving for Miami, a city neither had ever seen. Instead, by some arrangement no one quite understood, Eulalio began appearing at dawn with his own trays, and the two set their loaves side by side beneath the faded film posters. Customers came expecting quarrels. What they found was ______: Rosalinda lent him her oven at night, he shared his flour with her, and each recommended the other's pastries to anyone who asked.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: competition
suspicion
nostalgia
collaboration
items.explanation: 손님들은 20년 경쟁자인 두 사람이 다툴 것이라 기대했지만, 콜론 뒤에는 오븐을 빌려주고 밀가루를 나누며 서로의 빵을 추천하는 모습이 나온다. 이 구체적 행동들을 묶는 말은 협력이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 두 사람의 과거 관계에 끌린 오답이고, B는 손님들이 예상한 분위기와 혼동한 것이다. C는 낡은 영화 포스터 같은 배경에서 떠올릴 수 있지만 콜론 뒤 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Giacomo found the letters on a Tuesday, tied with fishing line in the bottom drawer of their mother's desk in the flat above the harbor in Naples. He waited until Zawadi arrived from Nairobi before opening them. The letters were from a man in Mombasa, and they spanned the four years before Zawadi was born. Their mother had never mentioned him. As Zawadi read aloud, Giacomo watched her face for anger, but what he saw was harder to name. She did not cry or put the pages down. Instead she read every line slowly, rereading certain sentences twice, her expression ______, as if each word confirmed something she had long suspected rather than revealed something new. Below the window, the fishing boats knocked gently against the quay.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: knowing
horrified
bored
puzzled
items.explanation: Zawadi는 울지도 편지를 내려놓지도 않고 천천히 읽으며, 빈칸 뒤에는 각 단어가 새로운 사실이 아니라 오래 짐작해 온 것을 확인해 주는 듯했다고 나온다. 따라서 이미 알고 있었다는 표정을 뜻하는 A가 정답이다. B는 Giacomo가 예상한 분노와 비슷한 반응으로, 울지 않았다는 단서와 맞지 않는다. C는 문장을 두 번씩 다시 읽는 집중과 어긋나고, D는 짐작이 확인되었다는 내용과 반대이다.

items.passage: When the first rain came to our hills north of Tehran that autumn, my brother Parvin and I stood in the doorway of our shop and argued about our father's rule. He had kept a tea garden on the slope behind us and a shop in front, and he had told us never to sell leaves picked after the first rain, for they were weak and bitter. But our father was ten years in his grave, the shop was nearly empty, and the late leaves hung thick on the bushes. Parvin said a rule made for a prosperous house need not bind a poor one. I was not so sure. That evening old Ofelia, who had bought from us since we were boys, tasted the new leaves and set down her cup. A rule, she said, is not ______ merely because the man who made it is gone; it lasts as long as its reason does.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: binding
void
useful
strict
items.explanation: 형제는 아버지가 세상을 떠났고 가게가 어려우니 규칙이 아직 유효한지 다툰다. Ofelia는 만든 사람이 사라졌다고 규칙이 그렇게 되는 것은 아니며, 이유가 남아 있는 한 지속된다고 말하므로 빈칸에는 무효라는 뜻의 B가 알맞다. A는 문장의 논리를 거꾸로 만든다. C와 D는 규칙의 성격을 말할 뿐 '지속된다'는 뒷부분과 대비를 이루지 못한다.

items.passage: Zaynab had swept the kite-maker's yard twice before the surveyor arrived, and she greeted him with a brisk, almost cheerful efficiency. Here were the bamboo frames, she explained, stacked by length; here the rice-paper sheets, dyed in the colors the festival committee in Manila had ordered. Nguyen made notes and nodded. She showed him the drying racks and the tins of glue, talking quickly, steering him always toward the left side of the yard. Then the wind shifted. From behind the shed came the soft, unmistakable rattle of a kite caught in the mango tree, the great dragon she had finished that morning, its spine already cracked. Zaynab stopped mid-sentence. Her voice, when it returned, was small and careful, and she no longer pointed at anything at all. Nguyen looked at the tree, then at her, and wrote nothing down.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From brisk confidence to subdued unease as a hidden flaw comes to light
From cheerful humor to open anger at the surveyor's intrusion
From anxious uncertainty to relief once the inspection is complete
From formal politeness to playful teasing between the two characters
items.explanation: 처음에 Zaynab는 활기차고 효율적으로 마당을 안내하면서도 늘 왼쪽으로만 측량사를 이끈다. 바람이 바뀌어 금이 간 용 연이 드러나자 그녀는 말을 멈추고 작고 조심스러운 목소리로 바뀐다. 따라서 자신감에서 위축된 불안으로 바뀌는 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 안도, D의 장난스러움은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage: Smell of wet soil and crushed shiso rose around them as Shigeru and Chiyo knelt in their plot of the community garden in Kyoto, pulling weeds between the rows of eggplant. For an hour they joked about their last concert, where the audience had numbered eleven, including a sleeping baby, and Chiyo imitated the hall manager's sigh until Shigeru dropped his trowel laughing. Then she mentioned the letter. A conservatory in Vienna had offered her a full scholarship beginning in January; it covered one student, not a duo. Shigeru went on weeding. He asked, evenly, when she would need to answer, and whether her cello would travel in the hold or on a seat. Each question was polite and practical, and each one seemed to set him a little further from her.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From bitter complaint about the concert to warm encouragement
From playful teasing to guarded restraint after Chiyo's news
From nervous tension to calm acceptance of a shared plan
From nostalgic reflection to open celebration of Chiyo's success
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 사람은 관객 열한 명이었던 공연을 두고 농담하며 웃는다. Chiyo가 혼자만 받을 수 있는 장학금 소식을 꺼내자 Shigeru는 담담하고 실무적인 질문만 하며 감정을 감춘다. 따라서 장난스러운 분위기에서 절제되고 경계하는 분위기로 바뀌는 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 격려나 축하를, C는 함께 세운 계획을 말하지만 지문의 거리감과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Once, I loved the library on Central Avenue
for its hush, its radiators ticking like patient clocks,
the way Elan would leave me in the stacks
and read the paper by the window, never hurrying.
We had a rhythm there: I chose, he signed.
Then on a Saturday in March he said,
between the atlases and the encyclopedias,
that he had sold the house, that we would move
to Denver in June, that it was settled.
Settled. As if I were a column he had added.
Now the radiators only hiss.
The books lean on each other like strangers in a line.
I, Nayeli, twelve, take down a map
and trace a road I did not choose.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the poem?
options: From restless boredom to eager curiosity about a new city
From quiet fear to comforting reassurance from Elan
From fond nostalgia to resentful bitterness after Elan's news
From playful humor to calm resignation about the move
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 도서관의 고요함과 Elan과의 리듬을 애정 어린 회상으로 그린다. Elan이 묻지도 않고 이사를 결정했다고 말한 뒤, 화자는 'Settled'를 되뇌며 자신을 더해진 숫자 한 줄에 비유하고, 라디에이터는 '쉭쉭거리기만' 한다. 따라서 애정 어린 그리움에서 원망 섞인 씁쓸함으로 바뀌는 C가 정답이다. D는 체념으로 보일 수 있지만 원망이 드러나는 표현을 놓쳤고, A와 B는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
BARTOLO: They printed your name alone, Judge, on the front page.
(Evening. The iron gate of a cemetery in Surabaya. LAN, a retired judge, leans on her cane. BARTOLO, her young clerk, holds a folded newspaper.)
LAN: (lightly) Newspapers like a single name. It fits the column better.
BARTOLO: I drafted three hundred pages of that opinion. You know I did.
LAN: (still amused) And I signed them. That is how it is done, my boy.
BARTOLO: My father is buried here. I promised him our family name would mean something one day. (He holds out the paper.) Read it to him.
(LAN stops smiling. A long pause. She takes the newspaper, studies it, then lowers it.)
LAN: (quietly) Give me your pen. Tomorrow I will write to the editor myself, and the correction will carry both our names.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From fierce anger to forced cheerfulness at the gate
From shared grief to hopeful celebration of the ruling
From formal respect to open hostility between the two
From dismissive amusement to sober acknowledgment of the clerk
items.explanation: 처음에 Lan은 '가볍게', '여전히 재미있다는 듯' 말하며 Bartolo의 기여를 관행이라고 넘긴다. Bartolo가 아버지의 무덤 앞에서 신문을 읽어 달라고 하자, 지문은 Lan이 웃음을 멈추고 오래 침묵한 뒤 '조용히' 말한다고 지시한다. 따라서 무시하는 듯한 여유에서 진지한 인정으로 바뀌는 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 분노, 축하, 적대감처럼 지문에 없는 감정을 내세운다.

items.passage: Three chairs, two mirrors, one radio tuned to the shipping forecast: that is the whole of Winston's barbershop on a narrow lane in Taipei, and for years I came less for the haircut than for his stories. He had been a sailor for thirty years, and he told those years like jokes: the typhoon off Okinawa, the cook who kept a parrot, the captain who could not swim. Last month, when I came in, Bokhee from the noodle stall next door was already in the chair, and Winston was laughing at something she had said. Then she asked about his nephew's boat, the one that had gone out in August and come back with half its crew. Winston set the scissors down. He finished her haircut without another word, and when I took her place, he cut my hair the way one folds a letter one does not want to reread.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From lively storytelling to heavy silence when a recent loss is raised
From bitter regret to amused acceptance of his years at sea
From casual friendliness to open anger at Bokhee's rudeness
From nervous chatter to calm confidence about his nephew's future
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Winston은 30년 항해를 농담처럼 들려주고 Bokhee의 말에 웃는다. Bokhee가 선원 절반을 잃고 돌아온 조카의 배를 묻자 그는 가위를 내려놓고 아무 말 없이 머리를 마저 자른다. 따라서 활기찬 이야기에서 무거운 침묵으로 바뀌는 A가 정답이다. B는 변화 방향이 반대이고, C의 분노와 D의 자신감은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.
